articles.title: Sinus Tarsi Approach With Distractor-Aided Reduction of Displaced Intra-articular Calcaneus Fracture.
articles.authors: Judson WR 4th, Ricci G
articles.population: Adults with displaced intra-articular calcaneus fractures
articles.outcomes: Wound complication rates, anatomical restoration, surgical timing
articles.take_home: The sinus tarsi approach using a distractor for calcaneus fracture repair may reduce wound complications and allow earlier surgery compared to the standard lateral approach, whilst still restoring the bone anatomy well.

articles.title: Reduction Techniques for Calcaneus Fractures-Using a Femoral Distractor.
articles.authors: Arnold JC, Druten E, Landis T, Lopas LA, Jang Y
articles.population: Adult with displaced intra-articular calcaneal fracture
articles.outcomes: Correction of coronal, sagittal, and axial malalignment; soft-tissue preservation
articles.take_home: A femoral distractor applied to the side of the heel bone can help straighten a displaced fracture whilst minimising damage to surrounding tissues during minimally invasive surgery.

articles.title: Supination Adduction Ankle Fracture Treated With Fibular Intramedullary Screw Fixation.
articles.authors: Di Pauli von Treuheim T, Cerasani MN, Konda S, Ganta A
articles.population: Patient with supination adduction ankle fracture
articles.outcomes: Successful open reduction and internal fixation with medial plafond disimpaction and cancellous allograft backfilling
articles.take_home: This case demonstrates a surgical technique for treating supination adduction ankle fractures that involves disimpacting the medial plafond, filling the bony void with allograft, and using a mini fragment plate for the medial malleolus combined with a retrograde screw for the lateral malleolus fracture.

articles.title: Ankle Syndesmotic Injury With Posterior Tibial Tendon Rupture.
articles.authors: Lezak BA, Mercer NP, Lowe DT, Egol KA
articles.population: Patient with ankle syndesmotic injury and posterior tibial tendon rupture
articles.outcomes: Identification of concomitant posterior tibial tendon rupture with syndesmotic injury; support for primary tendon repair
articles.take_home: This rare case of ankle syndesmotic injury combined with posterior tibial tendon rupture shows that doctors should carefully look for additional soft-tissue damage when patients have syndesmotic instability without fractures, and that primary tendon repair may be appropriate when rupture is found.

articles.title: Posterior Tibial Tendon Transfer and Achilles Tendon Lengthening for Foot Drop.
articles.authors: Mercer NP, Lezak BA, Lowe DT, Egol KA
articles.population: Patients with chronic post-traumatic foot drop from peroneal nerve injury
articles.outcomes: Restoration of ankle dorsiflexion and improved walking ability
articles.take_home: A surgical procedure that moves the posterior tibial tendon and lengthens the Achilles tendon can help restore ankle movement and improve walking in people with long-standing foot drop caused by nerve injury.

articles.title: Articular Reduction of a Bicondylar Tibial Plateau Fracture Using a Lateral Tibial Osteotomy.
articles.authors: Arnold JC, Druten E, Soni C, Suryavanshi J, Wynn M, Jang Y, et al.
articles.population: Adult with bicondylar tibial plateau fracture
articles.outcomes: Successful articular reduction and stable fixation using lateral tibial osteotomy approach
articles.take_home: A lateral tibial osteotomy can help surgeons directly see and lift a depressed joint surface when treating complex tibial plateau fractures without a natural split to access the damage. This technique allowed successful realignment and fixation in this case.

articles.title: Early Open Repair of a Multiligamentous Knee Injury.
articles.authors: Curran CC, Davis ME
articles.population: Patients with multiligamentous knee injuries from high-energy mechanisms
articles.outcomes: Surgical technique demonstration; postoperative weight bearing and knee range of motion outcomes
articles.take_home: Early open repair of multiple knee ligaments using the medial parapatellar approach may help selected patients recover faster and return to daily activities sooner. Patients can typically bear weight and move their knee immediately after surgery.

articles.title: The Modified Hardinge Approach to Hip Hemiarthroplasty: An Alternative in High-Risk Patients.
articles.authors: Beck A, Winzenried A, Beilfuss M, Dunahoe J
articles.population: High-risk patients undergoing hip hemiarthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Technique description and application of modified Hardinge approach
articles.take_home: The modified Hardinge approach using a direct lateral method may be an alternative surgical technique for high-risk patients needing hip hemiarthroplasty, accessing the hip through the front part of the gluteus medius muscle.

articles.title: Transradial Amputation With Nerve Management: Case Presentation and Surgical Technique.
articles.authors: Moll S, Dewing J, Bouz G, Hacquebord J, Ayalon O
articles.population: Adult with severe ballistic injury and complex regional pain syndrome
articles.outcomes: Phantom limb pain control, prosthetic function, residual limb stability and myoelectric signal quality
articles.take_home: A surgical approach combining nerve management techniques with careful limb positioning and muscle attachment improved pain control and prosthetic outcomes in one patient with a forearm amputation. The method aims to optimise functional recovery and quality of life after traumatic amputation.

articles.title: Carpal Tunnel Release: Technical Considerations for the Orthopaedic Trauma Surgeon.
articles.authors: Coscia A, Weinerman J, Hake M, Lawton J
articles.population: Patients with acute carpal tunnel syndrome secondary to distal radius fracture and/or compartment syndrome
articles.outcomes: Safety and efficacy of carpal tunnel release performed concurrently with fracture fixation and/or compartment release
articles.take_home: Carpal tunnel release can be performed safely and effectively at the same time as fracture fixation or compartment release surgery in patients with acute carpal tunnel syndrome from radius fractures, generally with good results.

articles.title: Intraarticular Distal Humerus With Anconeus Pedicle and Olecranon Osteotomy.
articles.authors: Cerasani MN, Zhang G, Konda S, Ganta A
articles.study_type: Case report and surgical technique review
articles.population: Patients with complex distal humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Accurate articular reduction and restoration of elbow function
articles.take_home: For complex broken elbows with severe fragmentation, surgeons can use a specialised technique involving extra small plates and a particular approach to the bone to improve how well they can put the pieces back together correctly.

articles.title: Humerus Shaft-Antegrade Intramedullary Nailing.
articles.authors: Karsmarski O, Stroh DA
articles.population: Patient with high-energy humeral shaft fracture and comorbidities
articles.outcomes: Surgical technique, setup considerations, and intraoperative methods for avoiding complications
articles.take_home: This review describes how to perform antegrade intramedullary nailing for humeral shaft fractures, including positioning, technique, and ways to prevent problems during surgery.

articles.title: AC Joint Reconstruction Using Cortical Suture Button and Semitendinosus Allograft.
articles.authors: Egol AJ, Lowe DT, Egol KA
articles.population: Patients with acromioclavicular joint injury
articles.outcomes: Clinical outcomes and biomechanical benefits of combined reconstructive technique
articles.take_home: This review describes a combined surgical technique using a cortical suture button and semitendinosus allograft for acromioclavicular joint reconstruction. Although no single technique has been shown to work better than others, this combined approach has theoretical biomechanical advantages.

articles.title: Comparison of Early Bracing Versus Splinting for the Initial Treatment of Acute Humeral Shaft Fractures (The COBRAS Trial).
articles.authors: Kingery MT, Ganta A, Egol KA
articles.population: Patients with acute closed humeral shaft fractures
articles.outcomes: Pain intensity, skin complications, opioid use, physical function, patient satisfaction over 10 days post-injury
articles.take_home: Starting treatment with a splint followed by a brace caused less pain and fewer skin problems than using a brace immediately. Both approaches gave similar pain relief and patient satisfaction.

articles.title: Incidence of nonunion after open tibia fractures in Malawi : associated factors and Radiographic Union Score for Tibial fractures reliability.
articles.authors: Schade AT, Dimock R, Mendes da Costa T, Nohakhelha N, Mwafulirwa K, Mkochi V, et al.
articles.population: Adults with open tibia fractures in Malawi
articles.sample_size: 287 participants enrolled; 177 with follow-up data at one year
articles.outcomes: Nonunion rate at one year; reliability of RUST score; association between RUST score and patient function (SMFA); comparison of treatment methods
articles.take_home: One in four patients with open tibia fractures in Malawi developed nonunion by one year, with significantly higher rates when fracture-related infection was present. The RUST scoring system reliably predicts patient function and healing even when radiograph quality is poor, helping clinicians decide when intervention may be needed.

articles.title: Is the use of retrospectively collected radiographic scores an accurate method to determine time to union? A retrospective clinical cohort.
articles.authors: Schlauch AM, Zakusylo A, Schaffer N, Mauffrey C, Hellwinkel JE, Ricci WM
articles.population: Adult patients aged 18 years and older treated with intramedullary nailing for acute tibial shaft fractures
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of time to union measured retrospectively using modified radiographic union scores for tibial fractures (mRUST); comparison of observed versus predicted time to union
articles.take_home: Using retrospective X-ray measurements with irregular follow-up intervals gave inaccurate estimates of healing time in patients with tibial fractures treated with intramedullary nailing, overestimating healing time by about 34 days. This study shows that retrospective radiographic assessments of bone healing are unreliable and should not be relied upon to determine when fractures have healed.

articles.title: Impact of MRI on the management of CT-defined AO spine A/B thoracolumbar fractures.
articles.authors: Quilichini JB, Dien E, Ranc PA, Kilani V, Pavan LJ, Desalos K, et al.
articles.population: Trauma patients with AO Spine A/B thoracolumbar fractures without neurological deficit
articles.outcomes: Change in treatment strategy after MRI; detection of posterior ligamentous complex injuries; occult spinal cord injury; agreement between CT and MRI fracture classification
articles.take_home: MRI changed the treatment plan in 12% of patients with thoracolumbar fractures, mostly by identifying injuries to ligaments at the back of the spine that CT had missed. This suggests MRI should be used selectively rather than routinely in these patients.

articles.title: Percutaneous fixation as definitive care for AO spine type B thoracolumbar fractures in polytrauma patients.
articles.authors: Giorgi PD, Ramponi A, Legrenzi S, Villa F, Boeris D, Picano M, et al.
articles.population: Polytrauma patients with AO Spine Type B thoracolumbar fractures
articles.outcomes: Operative time, blood loss, perioperative complications, radiological alignment, implant failure, hardware complications, and clinical outcomes at mean 2.6 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Percutaneous pedicle screw fixation was safe and effective for treating unstable thoracolumbar fractures in polytrauma patients, with no implant failures, infections or need for revision surgery at 2.6 years follow-up. This minimally invasive approach allowed early mobilisation and may be a suitable alternative to open surgery in these patients.

articles.title: Deep-learning CT reconstruction improves image quality but not diagnostic accuracy for sacral fragility fractures: MRI remains essential.
articles.authors: Naisan M, Brockstedt LA, Grebe AW, Joumah M, Kurz E, Hartung P, et al.
articles.population: Patients with pelvic CT examinations and corresponding MRI scans
articles.outcomes: Sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic accuracy for sacral fragility fracture detection; image quality and reader confidence
articles.take_home: New deep-learning CT reconstruction improved image quality and reader confidence, but did not improve the ability to detect sacral fragility fractures compared to standard CT. MRI remains necessary when sacral fracture is still suspected despite negative or unclear CT findings.

articles.title: Implementation of a thoracolumbar compression fracture remote review protocol safely reduces in-person spine consultations.
articles.authors: Nie J, Di Gerolamo J, Truong N, Grigorian A, Nguyen PD, Chan A, et al.
articles.population: Adult trauma patients with acute thoracolumbar compression fractures
articles.sample_size: 120 patients (79 in remote review group, 41 in bedside consultation group)
articles.outcomes: Incidence of thoracolumbar compression fracture-related complications, neurological deficits, brace-related complications, and time to discharge
articles.take_home: A remote review protocol by a spine surgery resident for non-operative thoracolumbar compression fractures was found to be safe, with no complications in either group and similar discharge times compared to traditional bedside consultations.

articles.title: Epidemiology and injury characteristics of pelvic ring injuries at a level 1 trauma centre: A 10-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Kumar PP, Ramesh P, Imran A, Devendra A, Dheenadhayalan J, Rajasekaran S
articles.population: Patients with pelvic ring injuries treated at a Level 1 trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Mortality, length of hospital stay, readmission, injury patterns, management type (operative versus non-operative), associated injuries, and complications
articles.take_home: Most pelvic ring injuries happened to young men in road traffic accidents and were usually the type that could be treated without surgery. About one in four patients had injuries affecting multiple body systems, which healthcare planners should account for.

articles.title: Placement of Triangular Titanium Implants Suprajacent to Pelvic Fixation Screws Reduces Pelvic Fixation Failure in Multilevel Spinal Fusion: Results of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Elder BD, Mundis G, Eastlack R, Arrigoni P, Franke J, Lee R, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing multilevel spinal fusion surgery with pelvic fixation for spine deformity
articles.outcomes: Pelvic fixation failure (screw breakage, lucency, pullout, or posterior rod breakage) at 24 months on radiographs and CT scan
articles.take_home: Adding triangular titanium implants above the pelvic screws reduced fixation failure from 20.4% to 11.0% in patients having multilevel spine fusion. This suggests the additional implants help protect against hardware problems at the point where the spine connects to the pelvis.

articles.title: Orthopaedic injuries among adults associated with electric skateboard use.
articles.authors: Katz R, Roche M, Kahn M, Karkenny A
articles.study_type: Retrospective database study using national emergency department surveillance data
articles.population: Adults aged 18 and over presenting to US emergency departments with electric skateboard, one-wheel, or longboard injuries
articles.outcomes: Fractures, dislocations, amputations, concussions, contusions, haematomas, strains, sprains, lacerations, punctures, crushing injuries, nerve damage and foreign bodies. Primary outcomes were fractures/dislocations and hospital admissions.
articles.take_home: Electric skateboard injuries in adults commonly result in fractures (especially to the clavicle, ankle and upper trunk), bruising and internal injuries. The researchers call for better safety measures including protective gear, although they note that effective prevention strategies for some injuries like clavicle fractures remain unclear.

articles.title: Intramedullary nail fixation for tibial plateau fractures: a systematic review of techniques and outcomes.
articles.authors: Box MW, Cooper JQ, Stanke J, Domingue GA, Dudoussat E, Puga TB, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of observational studies and case series
articles.population: Adults with tibial plateau fractures, predominantly bicondylar complex fractures
articles.sample_size: 205 patients across 10 included studies (52 with intramedullary nail alone, 45 with nail plus plate, 30 with nail plus condylar bolt, 78 with open reduction and internal fixation)
articles.outcomes: Infection rates (2.2-2.4%), bony union time (4 months or less), knee scores (good to excellent), malalignment (3 cases), knee pain (11-15.6%), no nonunion or malunion cases
articles.take_home: Intramedullary nailing with or without additional fixation appears to work as well as traditional open surgery for complex tibial plateau fractures. However, the evidence is still limited and more research is needed before these techniques can be recommended for all types of tibial plateau fractures.

articles.title: Periprosthetic fractures after hip and knee arthroplasty in France : national trends and future projections.
articles.authors: de Geofroy B, Bulsei J, Bouche PA, Micicoi L, Fontas E, Gonzalez JF, et al.
articles.population: Patients in France who needed surgery for fractures around hip or knee replacement implants
articles.sample_size: 15,029 periprosthetic fractures over ten years (2015 to 2024)
articles.outcomes: Incidence rates, mortality at three months and one year, postoperative complications, and projected fracture numbers to 2070
articles.take_home: Fractures around hip and knee replacements in France have doubled over the past decade and are expected to increase significantly by 2070 due to an ageing population. These fractures carry serious risks, with 16% of patients dying within a year and many experiencing complications like pressure ulcers and heart problems.

articles.title: Nine Months of Fluoxetine Aids in the Reduction of Posttraumatic Stress Symptoms following a Traumatic Musculoskeletal Injury: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Pazik M, Vasilopoulos T, de Faria L, Rijo D, Horodyski M, Mathews C, et al.
articles.population: Adults admitted to hospital with high-energy musculoskeletal trauma
articles.outcomes: Post-traumatic stress symptoms, pain, depression, anxiety, sleep quality and social function measured over 12 months
articles.take_home: Patients who took fluoxetine for 9 months after a serious musculoskeletal injury showed greater improvement in post-traumatic stress symptoms and pain compared to those who took a placebo. There were no significant differences between groups in depression, anxiety or social isolation.

articles.title: Serial drilling technique for sequential subtrochanteric femur fracture fixation in pediatric osteopetrosis: a technical report.
articles.authors: Mansour A, Wolf JJ, Slyepkan I, Turnow M, Anderson M, Wing A, et al.
articles.population: Paediatric osteopetrosis
articles.outcomes: Stable fracture fixation with no instrument failure or intraoperative complications
articles.take_home: A serial drilling technique using progressively larger drill bits with irrigation can safely fix fractures in children with osteopetrosis, avoiding the risks of drill breakage and accidental fractures that occur with traditional drilling methods.

articles.title: Comparing outcomes of acetabular fracture fixation in early career versus experienced orthopaedic trauma surgeons.
articles.authors: Davidson S, Flagstad I, Bober K, Carrazana-Suarez L, Vang S, Nguyen MP
articles.population: Patients aged 18 or older with acetabular fractures treated with open reduction internal fixation
articles.sample_size: 99 patients with 100 acetabular fractures (66 treated by early career surgeons, 34 by experienced surgeons)
articles.outcomes: Fracture reduction quality, operative time, blood loss, reoperations, 30-day mortality, hip survivorship, and HOOS JR functional scores at 1 year
articles.take_home: Patients treated by orthopaedic surgeons in their first 5 years of practice had comparable outcomes to those treated by surgeons with 10 or more years of experience, with similar fracture healing, functional recovery, and survival rates.

articles.title: Venous thromboembolism in children with lower limb fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Habib Z, Ahmed EM, Zipitis CS, Sutton PM, Malik RA, Charalambous CP
articles.population: Children aged 18 years or younger with lower limb fractures
articles.outcomes: Rate of venous thromboembolism, risk factors, mortality, and effectiveness of chemical thromboprophylaxis
articles.take_home: Blood clots in the legs or lungs occur in less than 1% of children with lower limb fractures, making them uncommon in this age group. However, there is not yet enough good quality evidence to say which children are at higher risk or whether preventative medicines are effective, so doctors should assess each child individually.
